_notes: **How to read this.** Each item was read against the source by a Sonnet subagent per language (one pass per language, the Rust draw repeated after the Rust oracle was fixed), with the cell's scope and the column's definition in hand; the main agent changed three Go verdicts (staticcheck's U1000 is transitive: a helper whose only caller is itself unused is dead by the tool's definition, so those are not oracle errors). **What the first draw found and what changed.** The first Rust draw had 19 oracle artefacts among 20 FN: trait-impl names were parsed with their `[Trait]` prefix so trait-declared methods lost their impls, serde/clap attribute uses inside strings were invisible, and bench / macro-registered tests were not roots. All three were fixed and the Rust sample re-drawn. **Known remaining oracle artefacts (listed in the samples above).** TypeScript: a helper reached only through dynamic indexing of a namespace import (`ns[tag]`) is reported unreachable (hono, 5 items). Rust: extension-trait methods called on foreign types (`SliceExt` on `&[u8]` in tokei, `Ordinal`/`Clean`/`CommandExt` in just) and helpers called only from `rgtest!`-generated tests are reported dead, because rust-analyzer's SCIP carries no occurrence for those calls (11 of the 20 Rust FN). Rust recall in the dead cells is therefore an upper-bound-of-the-oracle figure: some of its dead declarations are alive. Go: two buckets are conservative by rule (an exported method of an unexported type counts as public API; an exported symbol of an internal package is `exported_used_by_rule` in the unreferenced column).
